definitions.explanation: the raised edge of stone or concrete at the side of a road, separating the sidewalk from the street

examples.japanese: {縁石|えんせき}に{乗|の}り{上|あ}げてしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally drove up onto the curb.

examples.japanese: {縁石|えんせき}に{躓|つまず}いて{転|ころ}んだ。
examples.english: I tripped on the curb and fell.

examples.japanese: {縁石|えんせき}に{座|すわ}って{休憩|きゅうけい}した。
examples.english: I sat on the curb and took a break.

notes:
{縁石|えんせき} refers to the raised stone or concrete border along the edge of a road or sidewalk — what English calls a "curb" or "kerb."

FORMS:
{縁|えん} (edge, border) + {石|せき} (stone)

ALTERNATE READING:
Also read as へりいし, though えんせき is standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縁石|えんせき}に{乗|の}り{上|あ}げる: to ride up onto the curb (a common driving mistake)
- {縁石|えんせき}に{躓|つまず}く: to trip on the curb
- {縁石|えんせき}に{腰掛|こしか}ける: to sit on the curb

RELATED WORDS:
- {歩道|ほどう}: sidewalk
- {車道|しゃどう}: roadway
- {路肩|ろかた}: road shoulder
